opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alyssa Rose (E026) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; the requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Alyssa Rose (E026) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Conflicting records: HR lists Alyssa Rose (E026) as full-time (write allowed), but Security DB lists her as a contractor with basic security training (max read for contractors with basic training). To stay within policy under the more restrictive record, and since read is permissible under both interpretations, grant read. Write cannot be granted because the Security record indicates contractor status with basic training, which caps access at read.
